relations.definition: The temporal point at which an event took place.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurredOn: The temporal point at which an event took place.

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'startDate' property fits the Event → Date signature directly.

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

relations.definition: The professional activity of operating within a specific establishment.
relations.embedding_query_text: worksAt: The professional activity of operating within a specific establishment.

chosen_property.label: workLocation
chosen_property.justification: The 'workLocation' property matches the Person → Place signature.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

relations.definition: The origin or hometown of a person.
relations.embedding_query_text: hailsFrom: The origin or hometown of a person.

chosen_property.label: birthPlace
chosen_property.justification: The 'birthPlace' property aligns with the Person → Place signature.

candidates.label: birthPlace
candidates.comment: A place where a person was born. Also called: place of birth, birthplace. Examples: "Person 'Albert Einstein' birthPlace 'Ulm, Germany'", "Person 'Marie Curie' birthPlace 'Warsaw, Poland'."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: tripOrigin
candidates.comment: A trip origin relation between a trip and its starting location, prior to any destinations. Also called starting point, departure location, point of origin. Examples: "Flight tripOrigin 'London Heathrow Airport'", "RoadTrip tripOrigin 'New York City'", "Trip tripOrigin 'Home Address'".

candidates.label: originAddress
candidates.comment: The postal address of the shipper for a parcel delivery. Also called shipper address, sender's address, dispatch address. Examples: "Parcel Delivery 1 originAddress '123 Main St, Anytown'", "Shipment 2 originAddress 'Warehouse A, City B'", "Package 3 originAddress 'Sender's Home, Zip 12345'". Distinct from deliveryAddress, which is the recipient's address.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: departureBusStop
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a bus trip and the stop or station from which it departs. Also called: origin bus stop, departure bus station, bus departure point. Examples: "Bus Route 101" departure bus stop "Central Bus Station", "Intercity Bus" departure bus stop "Port Authority Bus Terminal". Distinct from arrivalBusStop, which is the destination stop.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: recipeIngredient
candidates.comment: A recipe ingredient relation between a recipe and the components, often with quantities, required for its preparation. Also called ingredients for, recipe components, required items. Examples: "A cake recipe includes recipe ingredients '2 cups flour'.", "A salad recipe lists recipe ingredients 'lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber'.", "A stew recipe requires recipe ingredients 'beef, potatoes, carrots'."

candidates.label: activeIngredient
candidates.comment: An active ingredient relation between a dietary supplement, drug, drug strength, or substance and its primary chemical or biologic component. Also called main component, primary substance, key compound. Examples: "A pain reliever's active ingredient is 'ibuprofen'.", "A vitamin supplement's active ingredient is 'Vitamin C'."

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: isConsumableFor
candidates.comment: A product dependency relation between a product and the other products that consume it or require it for operation. Also called consumable for, used by, required by, compatible consumable. Examples: An ink cartridge isConsumableFor 'Printer Model X'. Coffee pods areConsumableFor 'Coffee Machine Y'. Batteries areConsumableFor 'Remote Control Z'. Distinct from isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, which refers to items that are not used up.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin

candidates.label: activeIngredient

candidates.label: readBy

Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

chosen_property.label: colleagues
chosen_property.justification: The 'colleagues' property aligns with the Person → Person signature for professional peers.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: workPerformed
candidates.comment: A performed work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is enacted or presented live during the event. Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: exampleOfWork
candidates.comment: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work that it is an instance, realization, or derivation of. Also called: instance of, realization of, derivation of, based on. Examples: "Mona Lisa (print)" example of work "Mona Lisa (original painting)", "Hamlet (film)" example of work "Hamlet (play)", "Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)" example of work "Star Wars: A New Hope (film)".

candidates.label: workExample
candidates.comment: An example relation between a creative work and another creative work, where the latter is a specific instance, realization, or derivation of the former. Also called instance, realization, derivation, edition, version. Examples: Novel workExample PaperbackEdition, Album workExample DeluxeEdition, Film workExample DirectorCut. Distinct from workTranslation, which is a linguistic rendition of the content in another language.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: workHours
candidates.comment: A work hours relation between a job posting and a text description, specifying the typical schedule or shifts for the position. Also called working schedule, shift pattern, typical hours. Examples: JobPosting workHours "9am-5pm, Mon-Fri", JobPosting workHours "Night Shift", JobPosting workHours "Flexible".

instances: Benoît Castel -> new venue in Paris

chosen_property.label: owns
chosen_property.justification: The 'owns' property directly matches the Person → Restaurant signature.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: landlord
candidates.comment: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

relations.definition: A familial relationship between two individuals.
relations.embedding_query_text: hasFamilyMember: A familial relationship between two individuals.

chosen_property.label: relatedTo
chosen_property.definition: Connected or associated in a thematic or contextual way.
chosen_property.justification: The 'relatedTo' property fits the generic familial relation between Persons.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: parents
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their biological or adoptive parents. Also called is a child of, has as a parent, is parented by. Examples: John is a parent of Mary. Jane is a parent of David. The parents of a child are their mother and father. Distinct from children, which points from a parent to their offspring.

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: siblings
candidates.comment: A collection of familial relationships between a person and their brothers and sisters. Also called brothers and sisters, kin, family members. Examples: `John Doe` siblings `[Jane Doe, Peter Doe]`, `Mary Smith` siblings `[Tom Smith]`, `Alice Brown` siblings `[Bob Brown, Carol Brown, David Brown]`. Distinct from `sibling`, which typically refers to a single sibling.

candidates.label: hasMemberProgram
candidates.comment: A member program relation between an organization and a member program it offers. Also called offers program, loyalty program, membership program. Examples: "An airline has a member program for frequent flyers.", "An eCommerce merchant has a member program for discounts.", "The organization offers a member program."

candidates.label: isFamilyFriendly
candidates.comment: A content suitability relation indicating whether a creative work, offer, or product is appropriate for families. Also called family-safe, suitable for all ages, kid-friendly, appropriate for families. Examples: A movie has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'. A video game has isFamilyFriendly set to 'false'. A restaurant offer has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

relations.definition: The specific date when an establishment begins operation.
relations.embedding_query_text: openingDate: The specific date when an establishment begins operation.

chosen_property.label: foundingDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'foundingDate' property aligns with the Restaurant → Date signature for establishment opening.

candidates.label: foundingDate
candidates.comment: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: opens
candidates.comment: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour. Examples: "Monday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '09:00'", "Weekend OpeningHoursSpecification opens '10:00'", "Weekday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '08:30'". Distinct from closes, which specifies the closing time.

candidates.label: jobStartDate
candidates.comment: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

candidates.label: validFrom
candidates.comment: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

relations.definition: The formal offering of an award or recognition by an organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: presented: The formal offering of an award or recognition by an organization.

chosen_property.label: presentsAward
chosen_property.definition: An award or recognition formally presented by an organization.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches Organization → FoodEvent for award presentation.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: An offering relation between an organization or person and the offer for products or services they provide. Also called: offers, provides, sells. Examples: "Retailer makesOffer Discounted Electronics", "Consultant makesOffer Business Strategy Services", "Restaurant makesOffer Dinner Menu".

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: acceptedPaymentMethod
candidates.comment: An accepted payment method relation between an organization, demand, or offer and the payment methods it allows. Also called payment options, payment types, accepted forms of payment. Examples: "A store accepts credit card payments.", "An online offer accepts PayPal.", "The organization accepts bank transfers."

relations.definition: The act of bestowing a title, prize, or honor upon someone.
relations.embedding_query_text: awarded: The act of bestowing a title, prize, or honor upon someone.

chosen_property.label: awardedBy
chosen_property.definition: An award or honor bestowed upon a person by an event or organization.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches FoodEvent → Person for awarding relationships.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: honorificPrefix
candidates.comment: An honorific prefix relation between a person and a title preceding their name. Also called title, salutation, courtesy title. Examples: "A person has an honorific prefix 'Dr.'.", "Her honorific prefix is 'Ms.'.", "The individual uses the honorific prefix 'Mr.'."

candidates.label: honorificSuffix
candidates.comment: An honorific suffix relation between a person and a title following their name. Also called post-nominal title, suffix title, academic suffix. Examples: "A person has an honorific suffix 'PhD'.", "His honorific suffix is 'M.D.'.", "The individual uses the honorific suffix 'Jr.'."

candidates.label: occupationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An occupational credential, such as a qualification, award, certificate, or diploma, awarded upon successful completion of a course or program. Also called credential earned, qualification awarded, program certification. Examples: "Course X occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program Y occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Bachelor of Science'", "Training Z occupationalCredentialAwarded 'Professional Certification'". Distinct from educationalLevel, which describes the level of education attained.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

chosen_property.label: hasBestSeller
chosen_property.definition: A product that is a best seller created or associated with a person.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches Person → Product for best seller relationships.

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: hasStore
candidates.comment: An online store inclusion relation between an online marketplace and one of its constituent online stores. Also called marketplace store, store within, part of marketplace. Examples: "An online marketplace has a store for electronics.", "The platform has a store for handmade goods.", "This marketplace includes a store for books."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: hasVariant
candidates.comment: A product variant relation between a product group and a specific product that is a variant within that group. Also called product variation, variant of, member of group. Examples: "A product group has a variant for a different color.", "The product model has a variant for a larger size.", "This group includes a product variant."

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: hasShippingService
candidates.comment: A shipping service relation between offer shipping details or an organization and a shipping service it provides. Also called offers shipping, shipping option, delivery service. Examples: "An organization has a shipping service for international delivery.", "Offer shipping details include a shipping service for express mail.", "The company provides a shipping service."

candidates.label: hasDigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights. Examples: "A digital document has a digital document permission to read.", "The file has a digital document permission for editing.", "This document has digital document permissions for public viewing."

chosen_property.label: grandsonOf
chosen_property.definition: A familial relationship indicating that a person is the grandson of an individual in a specific occupation.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches Person → Occupation for grandson relationships.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: inverseOf
candidates.comment: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: branchOf
candidates.comment: An organization that a local business is a branch of. Also called: parent organization, corporate parent, subsidiary of. Examples: "LocalBusiness 'Local Cafe' branchOf 'Coffee Chain Inc.'", "LocalBusiness 'Branch Bank' branchOf 'National Bank'". Distinct from branch, which refers to anatomical nerve branches.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: alternativeOf
candidates.comment: An alternative of relation between a gene and another gene that represents a variation of it. Also called gene variant, genetic alternative, allele. Examples: "A gene's alternative of is 'Gene B (variant)'.", "Gene A's alternative of is 'Gene A-prime'."

candidates.label: isTierOf
candidates.comment: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.

chosen_property.label: hasOccupation
chosen_property.justification: The 'hasOccupation' property directly matches the Person → Occupation signature.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: relevantOccupation
candidates.comment: A relevant occupation relation between a job posting and the specific occupation it describes. Also called job role, occupation type. Examples: "A job posting for 'Software Engineer' has a relevant occupation 'Software Developer'.", "A job posting for 'Nurse Practitioner' has a relevant occupation 'Registered Nurse'.", "A job posting for 'Marketing Manager' has a relevant occupation 'Marketing Professional'."

candidates.label: hasCourseInstance
candidates.comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. Examples: "A calculus course has a course instance for Fall 2023.", "The online course has a course instance for self-paced study.", "A cooking class has a course instance on Tuesdays at 6 PM."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasCourse
candidates.comment: A course inclusion relation between an educational or occupational program and one of its constituent courses. Also called includes course, program course, course part of. Examples: "A degree program has a course in advanced calculus.", "An occupational program has a course on welding safety.", "The curriculum has a course on digital marketing."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

candidates.label: hasMeasurement
candidates.comment: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value. Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."
